title: Questionnaire fatigue is making third party risk data worse, not better
angle: Sending more questionnaires is actively degrading the answers you get back, at exactly the moment third party breaches are climbing. Good tension for a post.
keyPoints: Vendors are routinely asked to complete dozens and sometimes hundreds of security questionnaires a year, often duplicating each other.
Fatigued vendors rush, answer incompletely, or make errors, so the volume of assessment is degrading the quality of the data it produces.
Verizon's 2026 DBIR found third party involvement in breaches rose 60 percent, and breaches involving a third party now account for 48 percent of all breaches.
65 percent of large companies name third party and supply chain vulnerabilities as their biggest cyber resilience challenge, up from 54 percent the year before.
The UK NCSC reports only 14 percent of firms feel on top of the risks posed by their immediate suppliers.
The direction being pushed is contextual assurance: data driven signals instead of repeat questionnaires.

sources.title: Enhancing Third Party Risk Management: From Questionnaire Fatigue to Contextual Assurance
